rows.subtype: Approach: retracing the steps of the day [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl loses her water bottle and thinks back to where she had it last. She remembers drinking at PT class, goes back to the ground, and finds it on the bench.

rows.subtype: Approach: staying calm and thinking where he usually puts it [Thinking]
rows.description: A child takes a deep breath and thinks about where he normally keeps his house key. He checks the hook and the shoe rack, and finds it inside his shoe.

rows.subtype: Approach: searching the same place again and again [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy checks his school bag five times for a missing eraser. He feels sure it must be there, while he has not looked in his pencil case or pocket, and loses time and patience.

rows.subtype: Approach: deciding a place for each item to avoid losing [Revision]
rows.description: After losing three pencils in a week, a girl decides her pencil case always stays in the front pocket. She notices that most losses come from putting things down casually.

rows.subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
rows.subtype: Approach: staying calm and not replying in anger [Thinking]
rows.description: On seeing a private photo shared in a class group, a teen feels panic and rage, but decides that an angry reply would fuel it and that the first step is to gather help, not fight.

rows.subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
rows.subtype: Approach: blocking, muting and tightening privacy settings [Action]
rows.description: A teen blocks the harassing accounts, limits who can message or tag her, changes passwords, and asks friends not to forward anything, reducing exposure while the complaint proceeds.

rows.subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
rows.subtype: Approach: blaming the victim and hiding [Pitfall]
rows.description: A teen decides it is all her fault, deletes her accounts and avoids school, and the isolation cuts her off from the very people who could help stop the spread.

rows.subtopic: Handling a leaked photo or online harassment
rows.subtype: Approach: getting emotional support alongside practical steps [Revision]
rows.description: Days later, still sleeping badly, a teen notices the stress is not fading, tells the school counsellor, and adds regular talks with a trusted cousin to the plan instead of only handling logistics.

rows.subtype: Approach: calming down before deciding what to do [Thinking]
rows.description: After a fight over a borrowed pen, a girl feels hot with anger. She decides not to say anything then, sits with a book at lunch and thinks about it after she feels calmer.

rows.subtype: Approach: working out what actually happened [Thinking]
rows.description: A boy thinks back over the quarrel and realises he laughed when his friend dropped his tiffin, and the friend thought he was being mocked. Seeing the friend's side changes what he wants to say.

rows.subtype: Approach: waiting for the other friend to say sorry first [Pitfall]
rows.description: A girl thinks it was all her friend's fault and refuses to talk. Both wait for the other to speak first, and days pass while they feel lonely and their friends pick sides.

rows.subtype: Approach: asking a teacher for help to talk it out [Revision]
rows.description: Her first attempt to make up ends in shouting again. She notices they cannot fix it alone, so she asks the class teacher, who sits with both and lets each speak in turn.

rows.subtype: Approach: writing a list from the teacher's notice [Action]
rows.description: A boy reads the circular for the museum trip and lists lunch, water, cap, ID card and money. Using the notice as the source means he does not have to guess.

rows.subtype: Approach: imagining the day from morning to evening [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl walks through the trip in her mind, the bus, walking in the sun, lunch, and the ride back. She adds a hat, tissues and a plastic bag for wrappers.

rows.subtype: Approach: packing at the last minute in a hurry [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child begins packing at 6:30 am when the bus is due at 7. He forgets his permission slip and water bottle, and his mother has to run to the gate with them.

rows.subtype: Approach: learning from last year's trip and adjusting [Revision]
rows.description: A child recalls that last year she was thirsty because her small bottle finished by noon. This time she carries a bigger bottle and tells her friend to bring one too.

rows.subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
rows.subtype: Approach: sizing the fund from fixed monthly costs [Thinking]
rows.description: The person totals rent, food, EMIs and family support, multiplies by six, and treats the number as the target, then breaks it into a monthly saving goal.

rows.subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
rows.subtype: Approach: automatic transfer on salary day [Action]
rows.description: A standing instruction moves a fixed amount to a separate savings account the day salary arrives, removing the need for willpower each month.

rows.subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
rows.subtype: Approach: postponing until earning more [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person keeps saying that saving will start after a raise. Expenses rise with each raise, and a sudden hospital bill arrives before any reserve exists.

rows.subtopic: Building insurance and an emergency fund
rows.subtype: Approach: reviewing cover yearly [Revision]
rows.description: After a job change and a marriage, the person checks policy amounts and nominees, updating cover so that it matches new responsibilities rather than staying frozen from the first purchase.

rows.subtype: Approach: identify the underlying value behind the anger [Thinking]
rows.description: In a heated dinner debate over an election, the student asks what the uncle actually fears, such as safety for the family, and sees the difference behind the slogans. Looking for the value beneath a position opens room for dialogue.

rows.subtype: Approach: ask open questions to understand first [Action]
rows.description: The student asks a grandfather what experiences shaped his view and listens without interrupting, then shares one personal view calmly. Curiosity lowers defensiveness and may make later disagreement easier.

rows.subtype: Approach: win the argument with facts and links [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student pulls up statistics and forwards articles to prove the uncle wrong. Each fact hardens resistance because the exchange became a contest of status rather than a conversation.

rows.subtype: Approach: pause and take a break when emotions rise [Revision]
rows.description: Noticing a raised voice and a racing heart, the student says that the topic matters and suggests continuing after tea, then steps outside. Noticing the signs and pausing prevents a lasting quarrel.
